ID:Attribute.Definition: The name of a {c:bold}class{/c} that inherits from {c:color-white keyword}System.{/c}{c:color-green keyword}Attribute{/c}.{JumpExt}

ID:ClassDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}class{/c} declaration defines a blueprint for creating objects that contain data and behavior. It groups related variables and methods into a single reusable unit.{RefExt}

ID:ConstantDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}constant{/c} is a read-only value whose assigned value will never change. Constants are useful when the same literal value is reused in multiple places.

ID:ConstantReference.Definition: The name of a {c:color-white bold}constant{/c} field declared within the containing type.

ID:ConstructorDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}constructor{/c} is a special method that runs when a new instance of an object is created.{RefExt}

ID:ConstructorInvocation.Definition: The name of a type {c:bold}constructor{/c} being invoked in an object creation expression.{JumpExt}

ID:DelegateDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}delegate{/c} declaration defines a type that holds a reference to a method with a matching signature. Delegates are commonly used to store and invoke methods indirectly.

ID:EnumDeclaration.Definition: An {c:bold}enum{/c} declaration defines a set of named constants. It is commonly used to represent a fixed list of related values.

ID:EnumMemberDeclaration.Definition: An {c:bold}enum member{/c} declaration defines a single named value inside an enum. Each member represents one possible option from the enum.

ID:EventPropertyDeclaration.Definition: An {c:bold}event property{/c} declaration declares an event with explicit {c:color-blue keyword}add{/c} and {c:color-blue keyword}remove{/c} accessors that define custom subscription logic.

ID:EventFieldDeclaration.Definition: An {c:bold}event field{/c} declaration declares an event that uses a delegate type to manage subscriptions.

ID:FieldDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}field{/c} declaration defines a variable that belongs to a class or struct. Fields store data that represents the state of an object. By default, fields are only accessible from within the type they are declared in.

ID:FieldReference.Definition: The name of a {c:color-white bold}field{/c} declared within the containing type.

ID:GenericMethodDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}generic method{/c} declaration defines a method with one or more type parameters so the same method can work with different data types.{RefExt}

ID:GenericMethodInvocation.Definition: The name of a {c:bold}generic method{/c} being invoked in an invocation expression.{HovExt}

ID:InterfaceDeclaration.Definition: An {c:color-blue keyword}interface{/c} declaration defines a contract that specifies which members a conforming type must implement. Unlike a class, it contains only signatures with no implementation.{RefExt}

ID:LambdaParameter.Definition: The name of a {c:color-light-blue bold}lambda parameter{/c} that can be referenced inside the lambda expression it is declared in.

ID:LambdaParameterReference.Definition: The name of the {c:color-light-blue bold}lambda parameter{/c} declared before the lambda operator ({c:code}=>{/c}) in the current lambda expression.

ID:LocalFunctionDeclaration.Definition: The name of a {c:color-yellow bold}local function{/c}. A local function is declared inside another member or local scope and is only accessible within that containing scope.

ID:LocalVariableDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}local variable{/c} declaration defines a variable inside a method or block of code. Local variables are only accessible within the scope where they are declared.

ID:LocalVariableReference.Definition: The name of a {c:color-light-blue bold}local variable{/c} declared above within the containing scope.

ID:OutVariableReference.Definition: The name of a variable declared inline as an {c:color-blue keyword}out{/c} argument.

ID:MethodDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}method{/c} declaration defines a block of code that performs an action or returns a value. Methods are called to run the code they contain.{RefExt}

ID:MethodInvocation.Definition: The name of a {c:bold}method{/c} being invoked in an invocation expression.{HovExt}

ID:Parameter.Definition: The name of a {c:color-light-blue bold}parameter{/c} that is accessible anywhere within the following method or constructor body.

ID:ParameterReference.Definition: The name of a {c:color-light-blue bold}parameter{/c} defined in the containing method or constructor {c:tt color-light-blue}signature{/c}.

ID:ParameterLabel.Definition: The name of a {c:color-light-blue bold}parameter{/c} defined in the invoked method or constructor {c:tt color-light-blue}signature{/c}.

ID:PropertyDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}property{/c} declaration defines a member that provides controlled access to data on an object. Properties often include logic for getting or setting values.

ID:PropertyReference.Definition: The name of a {c:bold}property{/c} defined within the containing type.

ID:RecordDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}record{/c} declaration defines a reference type designed for storing data. Records provide built-in support for value-based equality and immutability.

ID:RecordStructDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}record struct{/c} declaration defines a value type designed for storing data. Record structs combine the efficiency of structs with record-style features.

ID:StructDeclaration.Definition: A {c:bold}struct{/c} declaration defines a value type that groups related data together. Structs are often used for small, lightweight data objects.

ID:GenericType.Definition: A type that must be supplied a {c:bold}generic type argument{/c}. The generic type argument passed in will replace the {c:bold}generic type parameter{/c} in the type definition.

ID:UsingResourceDeclaration.Definition: The name of a resource that will be automatically disposed at the end of the enclosing scope.
